title: Guide - Healing and Hope - Walking in peace

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Healing and Hope. <short pause> This practice is called Walking in Peace. <short pause> You can listen sitting still, or lying down, or on a slow walk. <short pause> Peace can travel at any speed.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Wherever you are, find the places where you meet the world. <short pause> The soles of your feet, perhaps. <short pause> Your back, or your hands. <short pause> Let your breath fall into an easy rhythm... <short pause> like footsteps that have nowhere they must be by a certain hour.

We sometimes think peace will come when the healing is finished. <short pause> When the grief is over, and the scar has faded, and we are who we were before. <short pause> But some losses go on being losses. <short pause> Some bodies mend slowly, or only in part. <short pause> Peace doesn't wait for all of that to be settled. <short pause> It is something you can be given... on the way.

An old priest named Zechariah learned this. <short pause> He had waited most of a lifetime for a child, and then spent long months unable to speak a word. <short pause> When his son was born, and his voice came back, he sang about the mercy of God... coming like sunrise. <short pause> His song ends this way, in Luke chapter one, verse seventy-nine.
To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He gives light to those who are sitting. <short pause> They haven't found their way out. <short pause> They haven't even stood up yet. <short pause> The morning comes to them where they are. <short pause> And then, so tenderly, He takes care of their feet... <short pause> and guides them into the way of peace.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So let's walk a little of that way, in your heart or with your feet. <short pause> One slow step, for where you have been. <short pause> Lord, You were there. <short pause> One slow step, for where you are. <short pause> Lord, You are here. <short pause> One slow step, for what you cannot see yet. <short pause> Lord, You will be there.

As you walk, what would you like to carry more lightly? <short pause> You don't have to put down the love, or the memory. <short pause> Those can come with you. <short pause> But perhaps there is some blame. <short pause> A question of what you should have done. <short pause> A date by which you thought you had to be well. <short pause> If you are willing, let one of those rest at the side of the road.

There will be mornings when you limp. <short pause> That is still walking. <short pause> There will be days you need to sit in the dark again for a while. <short pause> He knows how to find you there. <short pause> You can laugh without betraying what you lost. <short pause> You can cry without losing the ground you have gained. <short pause> Both belong on the way of peace.

Let's pray. <short pause> God of tender mercy, thank You for coming to me where I sit. <short pause> Shine on the next few feet of the road. <short pause> Heal what can be healed, and hold what cannot yet be. <short pause> Give me companions for the way... <short pause> and guide my feet, my slow and faithful feet, into Your peace. <short pause> Amen.

May the Lord give you light for the step in front of you. <short pause> May He give you mercy for the steps behind. <short pause> And wherever the road goes from here... <short pause> may you walk it in His peace.
